input.sql:
SELECT match_type
FROM marketing.ignore_list
WHERE
     (match_type = 'email'  AND lower(value) = :email)
  OR (match_type = 'domain' AND (lower(value) = :domain
                                 OR :domain LIKE '%.' || lower(value)))
  OR (match_type = 'prefix' AND :email LIKE lower(value) || '%')
  OR (match_type = 'suffix' AND :domain LIKE '%' || lower(value))
LIMIT 1

# ---- Safe parse: registration_answers may arrive as Array OR JSON string ----
raw = input["registration_answers"]
ra =
  if raw.is_a?(Array)
    raw
  elsif raw.is_a?(String) && !raw.strip.empty?
    (parse_json(raw) rescue [])
  else
    []
  end

# ---- YOUR logic: match by exact label ----
by_label = ->(label, key = "answer") {
  hit = ra.find { |a| a["label"] == label }
  hit && hit[key]
}

# ---- MY logic: match by question_type (stable across events) ----
by_type = ->(type, key = "answer") {
  hit = ra.find { |a| a["question_type"] == type }
  hit && hit[key]
}

# ---- MY logic: keyword fallback on label ----
by_keyword = ->(words, key = "answer") {
  hit = ra.find { |a|
    l = a["label"].to_s.downcase
    words.any? { |w| l.include?(w) }
  }
  hit && hit[key]
}

# treat empty strings as nil so fallbacks kick in
clean = ->(v) { (v.nil? || v.to_s.strip.empty?) ? nil : v }

# ===== EVENT ID (your logic) =====
event_id = input["url"].to_s.split("/").last

# ===== LINKEDIN =====
li = clean.(by_label.("What is your LinkedIn profile?")) ||
     clean.(by_label.("LinkedIn profile")) ||
     clean.(by_type.("linkedin")) ||
     clean.(by_keyword.(["linkedin"]))
linkedin =
  if li.nil?
    nil
  elsif li.start_with?("http")
    li
  else
    "https://www.linkedin.com" + (li.start_with?("/") ? li : "/#{li}")
  end

# ===== COMPANY =====
company = clean.(by_label.("Where do you work?")) ||
          clean.(by_label.("What company do you work for?")) ||
          clean.(by_type.("company", "answer_company")) ||
          clean.(by_type.("company")) ||
          clean.(by_keyword.(["company", "where do you work", "employer"]))

# ===== JOB TITLE =====
job_title = clean.(by_label.("What is your job title?")) ||
            clean.(by_label.("What company do you work for?", "answer_job_title")) ||
            clean.(by_type.("company", "answer_job_title")) ||
            clean.(by_keyword.(["job title", "role title", "your role"]))

# ===== COUNTRY =====
country = clean.(by_label.("What country are you from?")) ||
          clean.(by_label.("Where are you from?"))        ||
          clean.(by_label.("Country of residence"))        ||
          clean.(by_keyword.([
            "what country", "which country", "country",
            "where are you from", "where are you based",
            "based in", "residence", "nationality"
          ]))
country = "United Kingdom" if country == "United Kingdon"

# ==========================================================
# ===== BLOCKED COUNTRIES (new input) =====
# ==========================================================
raw_bc = input["blocked_countries"]
blocked_list =
  if raw_bc.is_a?(Array)
    raw_bc
  elsif raw_bc.is_a?(String) && !raw_bc.strip.empty?
    (parse_json(raw_bc) rescue [])
  else
    []
  end
blocked_list = [] unless blocked_list.is_a?(Array)

# normalize: lowercase, trim, collapse spaces
norm = ->(v) { v.to_s.strip.downcase.gsub(/\s+/, " ") }

country_n = norm.(country)

matched_block =
  if country_n.empty?
    nil
  else
    blocked_list.find { |b|
      next false unless b.is_a?(Hash)
      b_name = norm.(b["country"])
      b_iso  = norm.(b["country_iso_code"])
      (!b_name.empty? && b_name == country_n) ||   # "Russia" == "Russia"
      (!b_iso.empty?  && b_iso  == country_n)      # answer was "RU"
    }
  end

country_blocked     = !matched_block.nil?
blocked_country_iso = country_blocked ? matched_block["country_iso_code"] : nil

# ==========================================================
# ===== email/domain + ignore decision (from Postgres) =====
# ==========================================================
full_email = input["user_email"].to_s.strip.downcase
domain     = full_email.include?("@") ? full_email.split("@").last : ""

# These come from the Postgres "Run custom SQL" step BEFORE this Ruby step:
#   pg_match_count -> number of rows returned (0 or 1)
#   pg_match_type  -> the matched 'match_type' value (nil/empty if none)
pg_match = input["pg_match_count"].to_i > 0

# ===== Combine ignore reasons =====
reasons = []
reasons << (clean.(input["pg_match_type"]) || "email_match") if pg_match
reasons << "blocked_country: #{country}"                     if country_blocked

should_ignore = !reasons.empty?
ignore_reason = should_ignore ? reasons.join(" | ") : nil

{
  "event_id"                  => event_id,
  "event_name"                => input["name"],
  "first_name"                => input["user_first_name"],
  "last_name"                 => input["user_last_name"],
  "email"                     => input["user_email"],
  "phone_number"              => input["phone_number"],
  "hs_linkedin_url"           => linkedin,
  "company"                   => company,
  "job_title"                 => job_title,
  "country"                   => country,
  "luma_last_checked_in_date" => input["check_in_date"],

  "email_domain"              => domain,
  "should_ignore"             => should_ignore,
  "ignore_reason"             => ignore_reason,

  # NEW outputs
  "country_blocked"           => country_blocked,
  "blocked_country_iso"       => blocked_country_iso
}

properties.label: Clearout AI Verdict
properties.hint: AI verdict on the email's likely validity.
properties.name: co_aiverd

properties.label: Clearout Email Reason
properties.hint: The sub-status explaining why the email received its verification result. Use this to understand and triage invalid or risky emails before deciding how to act on them.
properties.name: co_dp_e_reason

properties.label: Clearout Email Safe To Send
properties.hint: Indicates whether the contact's email is safe to send to, based on its verification result. Use this to filter out the emails that are guaranteed to deliver with out bounce by choosing safe to send as 'yes'
properties.name: co_dp_e_safe

properties.label: Clearout Email SMTP Provider
properties.hint: The SMTP / email service provider hosting the email's domain (e.g. Google, Microsoft). Use this to spot provider-specific deliverability patterns and tailor your sending strategy.
properties.name: co_dp_e_smtp

properties.label: Clearout Email Status
properties.hint: The email verification status — valid, invalid, catch-all or unknown. Use this to segment contacts by deliverability and decide which emails are worth contacting.
properties.name: co_dp_e_status

properties.label: Clearout Name Gibberish
properties.hint: Indicates whether the contact's name looks like gibberish (random or meaningless characters). Use this to flag low-quality or fake records and keep your CRM data clean.
properties.name: co_dp_n_gibberish

properties.label: Clearout Name Status
properties.hint: The name validation status for the contact. Use this to assess given value belongs to person name or not.
properties.name: co_dp_n_status

properties.label: Clearout Phone Carrier
properties.hint: The telecom carrier that owns the phone number. Use this for carrier-aware routing, cost optimization or compliance checks.
properties.name: co_dp_p_carrier

properties.label: Clearout Phone Country Name
properties.hint: The country the phone number belongs to. Use this for geographic segmentation and region-based campaigns.
properties.name: co_dp_p_country_name

properties.label: Clearout Phone Country Timezone
properties.hint: The timezone of the phone number's country. Use this to schedule calls or texts at an appropriate local time and improve response rates.
properties.name: co_dp_p_country_timezone

properties.label: Clearout Phone DST Observed
properties.hint: Indicates if Daylight Saving Time (DST) is active. Use this to adjust your calling time and avoid dialing too early or late.
properties.name: co_dp_p_dst

properties.label: Clearout Phone E164 Format
properties.hint: The phone number in standardized E.164 international format. Use this for reliable dialing across regions and de-duplication of contact records.
properties.name: co_dp_p_e164_format

properties.label: Clearout Phone Line Type
properties.hint: The phone line type — mobile, fixed line, VoIP, etc. Use this to target SMS-capable mobile numbers and pick the right channel for outreach.
properties.name: co_dp_p_line_type

properties.label: Clearout Phone Location
properties.hint: The geographic location associated with the phone number. Use this for region-based targeting and localized outreach.
properties.name: co_dp_p_location

properties.label: Clearout Phone Status
properties.hint: The phone number validation status. Use this to filter out unreachable numbers before dialing or texting and avoid wasted outreach.
properties.name: co_dp_p_status

properties.label: Clearout Pulsed On
properties.hint: The date and time the contact was last enriched by Data Pulse. Use this to identify stale records that are due for a refresh.
properties.name: co_dp_pulsed_on

properties.label: Clearout Ref ID
properties.hint: Reserved for future use
properties.name: co_dp_ref_id

properties.label: Clearout MX Record
properties.hint: MX record found for the email's domain.
properties.name: co_mxrec

properties.label: Clearout Email Status
properties.hint: The email verification status — valid, invalid, catch-all or unknown. Use this to segment contacts by deliverability and decide which emails are worth contacting.
properties.name: co_dp_e_status

properties.label: Clearout Name Gibberish
properties.hint: Indicates whether the contact's name looks like gibberish (random or meaningless characters). Use this to flag low-quality or fake records and keep your CRM data clean.
properties.name: co_dp_n_gibberish

properties.label: Clearout Name Status

properties.name: co_dp_n_status

properties.label: Clearout Phone Carrier
properties.hint: The telecom carrier that owns the phone number. Use this for carrier-aware routing, cost optimization or compliance checks.
properties.name: co_dp_p_carrier

properties.label: Clearout Phone Country Name
properties.hint: The country the phone number belongs to. Use this for geographic segmentation and region-based campaigns.
properties.name: co_dp_p_country_name

properties.label: Clearout Phone Country Timezone
properties.hint: The timezone of the phone number's country. Use this to schedule calls or texts at an appropriate local time and improve response rates.
properties.name: co_dp_p_country_timezone

properties.label: Clearout Phone DST Observed
properties.hint: Indicates if Daylight Saving Time (DST) is active. Use this to adjust your calling time and avoid dialing too early or late.
properties.name: co_dp_p_dst

properties.label: Clearout Phone E164 Format
properties.hint: The phone number in standardized E.164 international format. Use this for reliable dialing across regions and de-duplication of contact records.
properties.name: co_dp_p_e164_format

properties.label: Clearout Phone Line Type
properties.hint: The phone line type — mobile, fixed line, VoIP, etc. Use this to target SMS-capable mobile numbers and pick the right channel for outreach.
properties.name: co_dp_p_line_type

properties.label: Clearout Phone Location
properties.hint: The geographic location associated with the phone number. Use this for region-based targeting and localized outreach.
properties.name: co_dp_p_location

properties.label: Clearout Phone Status
properties.hint: The phone number validation status. Use this to filter out unreachable numbers before dialing or texting and avoid wasted outreach.
properties.name: co_dp_p_status

properties.label: Clearout Pulsed On
